project_overview: This Vue.js application appears to be a complex educational platform, likely focused on student progress tracking and learning resources. The application utilizes a layered architecture with distinct views managing various aspects of the user experience, including exam submissions, results, and personalized learning.  The dependency graph reveals a tight coupling between several views, particularly around the ‘ResultPage’ functionality.  The presence of several ‘iLike’ views suggests a personalized learning component.

layers.description: Handles user interface and user interactions.  Relies heavily on routing and data presentation.
Responsible for handling data retrieval and manipulation. Not explicitly defined, but inferred from routing dependencies.

macro_trends.title: High-Level View Dependency Overload
macro_trends.description: Several high-level Vue components (e.g., ResultPage, ExamFormSubmission) are directly linked to numerous lower-level components (e.g., ApplicationServices, Transactions), creating a potential single point of failure and impacting maintainability. This suggests a need for a more modular architecture.

macro_trends.title: Potential UI/UX Inconsistencies
macro_trends.description: Multiple views are directly importing from others and sharing common UI elements, creating a risk of inconsistent design and potential UX issues. Careful review of styling and component structure is needed.

key_workflows.name: Exam Submission Workflow
key_workflows.description: This workflow maps the flow from submission of an exam form (ExamFormSubmission) through data processing (Transactions) and finally displaying the results (ResultPage). The dependency chain suggests a potential bottleneck in the transaction processing phase.

key_workflows.name: Result Display Workflow
key_workflows.description: This workflow connects user interactions (via various Vue components like ResultPage) to the underlying data storage and display. The routing dependencies highlight a key area for optimization and potential performance issues.
